title: Nine calls that came out of the 2026-10-25 batch
intro: Draft. Published once sheet 1 is answered; any sheet 1 card you marked Later is added to it then. Same rules: tap the recommendation or another option, notes optional, nothing applied until you say yes.

items.name: Render-target rule counted in full-screen equivalents
items.question: Performance rule 10 caps the pack at six render targets. Clouds, light shafts, bloom and ambient occlusion each want a quarter- or half-resolution buffer.
items.context: Counting buffers by full-screen bandwidth equivalents keeps the rule's intent (memory and bandwidth) while letting the four sub-resolution passes in: today's six buffers are 4.1 equivalents; all four additions together add about 0.3. The alternative keeps the literal count and the four passes share or drop buffers.

options.label: Count in full-screen equivalents
options.desc: Cap stays at the equivalent of six full-screen buffers.

items.why: Same budget, measured honestly; the passes that improve the look most need it.

items.name: The old F32 Modded Edition for 1.7.10
items.question: A community pack from the Faithful era covers Railcraft, Twilight Forest, Witchery, Chisel, Storage Drawers, Iron Chests, ProjectE and Biomes O' Plenty at 32x. Its only licence is a README sentence: use or modify in any way, no profit from distribution. No LICENSE file, not the Faithful License.
items.context: Taking it would fill most of the top-150 modded blocks at once with per-file source records. The look bible's rule is that nothing ships unless it is licensed for derivatives; a README sentence is a permission, but a thin one. Without it those blocks stay at 16x until drawn.

options.label: Use it, with the README quoted as the licence
options.desc: Per-file source records, credit in CREDITS.txt.

options.label: Reference only
options.desc: Stay at 16x; draw our own over time.

items.why: The permission is explicit and non-commercial use is all we do; it is the only way to 32x those mods this year.

items.name: Netherrack and end stone in QF Textures
items.question: QF v0 keeps netherrack and end stone at vanilla 16x. The Nether and End ores can only be re-composited on Faithful 32x hosts if those two move to Faithful too.
items.context: Faithful's netherrack and end stone are the same designs with more detail, like its stone. Moving them changes the look of two whole dimensions; keeping them leaves their ores at 16x beside 32x stone ores.

options.label: Faithful 32x for both
options.desc: Nether and End ores follow the stone-ore path.

items.name: Four uncertain backport matches
items.question: Legends' and Chisel's backported vanilla blocks were mapped to modern Faithful by colour match. Four did not match closely: soul fire (two frames, Faithful's is a different drawing), silver concrete (not Faithful's light-gray), blast furnace bottom.
items.context: They were left out of the build. Taking them means a visible design change on those four; leaving them keeps 16x there.

groups.name: Questline: WP-6 proposals
groups.blurb: From the WP-6 draft (tools/quests/drafts/DefaultQuests.wp6.json), built from the Act I answers. These are its two balance proposals and one structural choice.

items.name: Finale and Pack Master rewards
items.question: Each act finale (481, 484, 485, 486) rewards one loot bag and one sealed tome of the act's tier (Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary); Pack Master (63) rewards a statue and one Legendary bag.
items.context: All inside the audit's reward band for each act. Alternatives: finales reward nothing but the next act (the kill was the reward), or a cosmetic only.

options.label: Bag and tome per finale, as drafted
Cosmetic only
options.desc: A trophy or statue per finale, no loot.

options.label: No finale rewards
options.desc: Opening the next act is the reward.

items.name: Act III hands out 78 diamond-equivalents against a budget of 72
items.question: Merging the End and OreSpawn chapters into one act puts their existing rewards together over the budget by six.
items.context: Nothing new was added; these are pre-existing rewards now counted in one act. Trimming six diamonds from the End chapter's rewards fixes it; accepting it leaves the ladder as it was.

options.label: Trim six from the End chapter
options.desc: Say which quest in the note, or leave it to the writers.

items.name: When the Act III tab first shows
items.question: 94 Knight Phantom still needs 17 Hydra, so the Act III tab unlocks at the Hydra, before the Act II finale (484) is done.
items.context: One prerequisite change (94 needs 484) makes Act III appear only after Act II's finale. Leaving it gives players a peek at the next act while they finish Witchery.

options.label: Leave the peek
options.desc: Act III shows at the Hydra.

items.why: Every other act boundary is a finale; one exception reads as a mistake.

items.name: Remote console over Tailscale
items.question: Today every admin action means sitting at the host PC. RCON bound to a Tailscale (or ZeroTier) private network lets you and one co-admin run list, say, whitelist, kick and ban from a phone or laptop.
items.context: Free; the RCON password is plaintext so it must never be port-forwarded; in 1.7.10 RCON commands run off the main thread, so stop and save stay with the supervisor. Needs Tailscale installed on the host and on each admin device.

options.label: No remote console
options.desc: Admin at the host PC, or through the supervisor inbox.

items.name: Nine quests ask for things the data says a player cannot get
items.question: Spirit World (45) asks for a technical block, Trophy Hunter (53) for a statue with no recipe, 120 for a hidden biome core, three TragicMC key quests (134, 135, 144) for creative-only keys, 432 for the Sync Core (recipe registered per world, maybe fine), 440 for a creative-only banner.
items.context: qb.py now warns on all nine. Each needs a hand check in game before editing: some may have recipes the item dump missed. The fixes would be a location task for 45, a reward-provided or recipe-added item for the rest.

options.label: Verify in game, then fix each
options.desc: A PC agent checks; writers fix the texts.

options.label: Fix from the data now
options.desc: Trust the census; change the tasks.
